articles.title: Japan Smashes Its Own Heat Record as Summer Temperatures Soar Past 40°C
articles.summary: A city in Japan's Kumamoto Prefecture has broken an extraordinary temperature record, reaching 40.3 degrees Celsius — the very first time the region has ever gone above 40 degrees in recorded history. The Japan Meteorological Agency issued urgent warnings, asking the public to guard against heatstroke. Scientists say these extreme heat events are growing more frequent across Asia because of ongoing climate change. Health authorities are particularly concerned about children and elderly people, advising everyone to stay cool indoors, drink water regularly, and limit time spent outside during the hottest hours. The record was set in the early afternoon on a Monday.

lv1: What is the highest temperature that was recorded in Kumamoto, Japan, during this heatwave? (日本熊本在今次熱浪中錄得的最高溫度是多少？)
What did the Japan Meteorological Agency ask people to watch out for during the hot weather? (日本氣象廳呼籲市民在炎熱天氣下要注意什麼？)
lv2: Why do scientists believe that extreme heatwaves like this one are happening more and more often in Asia? (科學家為何認為像這次一樣的極端熱浪在亞洲愈來愈頻繁？)
Why are children and elderly people considered especially at risk during a heatwave, and what should they do to stay safe? (為什麼兒童和長者在熱浪期間被認為特別危險？他們應該怎樣保護自己？)
lv3: Who do you think should be most responsible for protecting people from heatwaves — the government, businesses that contribute to climate change, or individuals themselves? Give reasons for your view. (你認為誰應該對保護市民免受熱浪傷害負最大責任——政府、導致氣候變化的企業，還是市民個人？請說明你的理由。)

If temperatures in Asian cities keep rising every summer, what changes should governments and city planners make to keep people safe? What difficulties might they face in doing so? (如果亞洲城市的夏季氣溫持續上升，政府和城市規劃者應作出哪些改變來保障市民安全？他們在推行這些措施時可能面對什麼困難？)

articles.title: Hong Kong University Places More Competitive Than Ever as JUPAS Results Released
articles.summary: Hong Kong's university admission results under JUPAS have been announced, showing that competition for places is fiercer this year due to a rise in the number of applicants. The Chinese University of Hong Kong accepted roughly 63% of its medical students through JUPAS, maintaining a higher rate than the University of Hong Kong's 51.7% for the ninth year in a row. Education advisors are urging students who missed out on their preferred courses to consider the approximately 30 self-financing institutions offering sub-degree and bachelor programmes. Experts say careful planning and applying to multiple types of programmes gives students the best chance of continuing their studies at a higher level.

lv1: What is the name of Hong Kong's university admissions system mentioned in the article? (文章中提到的香港大學入學申請系統叫什麼名稱？)
For how many years in a row has CUHK had a higher JUPAS medical admission rate than HKU? (中大的JUPAS醫科取錄率連續多少年高於港大？)
lv2: Why is it important for students to apply to more than one type of university programme when submitting their JUPAS choices? (為什麼學生在填寫JUPAS選擇時，申請多於一種類型的課程是重要的？)
What is the difference between a self-financing institution and a government-funded university in Hong Kong, and why might a student choose one over the other? (香港自資院校與政府資助大學有什麼分別？學生為何可能選擇其中一種？)
lv3: Is it fair that a student's entire university future can depend mainly on exam results from a single set of public examinations? What are the arguments for and against this system? (一個學生的大學前途主要取決於一次公開考試的成績，這樣公平嗎？這個制度有哪些支持和反對的理由？)

Should Hong Kong increase the number of government-funded university places to reduce competition and stress on students, or would this reduce the value and quality of a degree? Discuss both sides. (香港應否增加政府資助大學學額，以減少學生競爭和壓力？這樣做會否降低學位的價值和質素？請討論正反兩面。)

articles.title: 「Fun Coffee」虛幣騙案拘8人　涉款近億　港澳逾230宗報案
articles.summary: 警方就「Fun Coffee」加密貨幣投資騙案展開行動，逮捕8名涉案人士。騙徒聲稱投資與「咖啡科研」有關的虛擬貨幣，以高達四倍回報為餌誘騙市民，令不少人損失金錢。案件涉及金額接近一億港元，香港及澳門合共有234宗相關報案。警方提醒市民，遇到聲稱高回報的投資計劃，必須提高警惕，不應輕信陌生人推薦或網上廣告，遇有懷疑應向警方舉報，保障自己的財產安全。

lv1: 騙徒以什麼作為誘餌，吸引市民參與「Fun Coffee」投資？
「Fun Coffee」騙案在香港及澳門合共有多少宗報案？
lv2: 為什麼「高回報」的投資宣傳往往是騙局的警號？遇到這類情況應如何應對？
執法機關可以採取哪些措施，防止加密貨幣騙案繼續發生？
lv3: 有觀點認為被騙者需要為自己的損失負一定責任，因為高回報必伴隨高風險，是投資常識；另一觀點則認為責任完全在於騙徒。你認同哪個立場？原因是什麼？
政府應否對加密貨幣投資平台實施更嚴格的監管和牌照制度？這樣做會帶來哪些好處，又可能產生哪些問題？

articles.title: 內地牛蛙抗生素超標逾五倍　禁用獸藥現蹤　專家警告具致癌風險
articles.summary: 內地傳媒與公益機構聯合展開長達一個月的食品安全調查，發現福建、廣東及江蘇等地出售的牛蛙產品，抗生素含量最高超出標準五倍有多。更嚴重的是，部分樣本驗出國家禁止用於食用動物的獸藥「呋喃唑酮」，專家警告此物質可致癌及引起發育問題。調查同時揭露部分加工廠以假樣本欺騙政府抽查。由於不少港人北上用餐時愛點牛蛙菜式，消費者應特別注意飲食安全，選擇來源可靠的食材。

lv1: 調查在牛蛙產品中發現了哪種有害物質？
今次食品安全調查涵蓋內地哪幾個省份？
lv2: 為什麼部分食品加工廠要使用「假樣本」應付政府的食品安全抽查？這反映了什麼問題？
長期攝入含有超標抗生素或禁用獸藥的食物，對人體健康可能造成哪些長遠影響？
lv3: 有人認為食品安全責任主要在於生產商和監管機構，消費者只是受害者；也有人認為消費者選擇時也應多加謹慎。你認為各方應如何分擔責任？
食品安全問題一再出現，單靠加重罰則是否足夠？還需要哪些更根本的改變，才能有效保障公眾健康？
